Lift the open right gripper clear of the holder before making further lateral alignment corrections; the cup is not yet centered between the jaws.

Bring the oblique grasp slightly toward the near side of the fallen holder and close around its middle. Retention remains to be checked by lifting.
Keep the right gripper closed and lift the holder clear of the table while retracting slightly. Check whether it remains between the jaws before uprighting.
The holder stayed on the table, so the grasp missed. Reopen and move the right grasp center left and farther forward over its new location before descending.
Lower the open right gripper with a small left/forward correction so the fallen holder is deeper between the jaws rather than contacted at an edge.
Fine-align the right grasp slightly right and forward, lower around the holder's near half, then close. Verify retention on the next lift.
Keep the right gripper fully closed and lift/retract to test retention of the holder before rotating it upright.
The holder was not retained. Reopen and correct substantially left/forward toward its visible center, using a more downward approach rather than pinching its edge.
Replan from the executed prefix without further wrist rotation. Lower and shift left to surround the holder's near end, then close the right gripper.
The holder is still ahead of the jaws. Change to a shallower forward grasp from its near end, lowering the wrist while rotating the open fingers forward to gain reach without extending the arm.
The larger change was rejected. Retract slightly and start the shallower approach with very small rotation increments to maintain the current elbow-up branch.
Neither rejected chunk moved. Use tiny retraction and pitch increments to move away from the sensitive reach boundary before any further descent.
Continue making the right grasp shallower while lowering toward the holder's near end. Keep the jaws open until the holder is visibly between them.
The fingertips appear below and short of the holder's near end. Raise slightly while advancing the open jaws, then close around that end.
Test the new end grasp by lifting and retracting with the right gripper fully closed, keeping the holder clear of the table before uprighting.
Retention failed again. Reopen and approach the holder farther to the right of the previous pinch, targeting its middle rather than the visible near corner.
Advance the open jaws farther along the holder, with a slight right correction and small descent, to obtain a deeper body grasp.
Close at the deeper alignment and perform a short upward/rearward retention test. Keep the right gripper at zero during the lift.
The holder remains beyond the closed jaws. Reopen, lift clear, and rotate the right grasp to better match the holder's diagonal long axis before another approach.
With the jaws aligned across the holder, descend toward its body and advance only slightly. Keep open and check alignment before closing.
The holder is still ahead of and below the grasp center. Advance and lower the open right jaws farther, with a small left correction, without changing wrist orientation.
Forward reach was interrupted after two steps. Switch to a shallower end approach, lowering and retracting the wrist while rotating the open fingertips forward to preserve reach margin.
The holder's near end is now visible between the open fingers. Correct slightly left and down, then close around its sides without advancing enough to push it away.
Lift and retract gently with the right gripper closed to check whether the holder's near end is retained.
The end grasp was too shallow. Reopen, lower to the holder's side height, and advance farther so its body—not only the end face—can enter between the fingers.
Advance another short distance at the holder's side height, slightly left to center the end face, then close the right jaws around the near body.
Forward motion stopped before closure. Close at the current deeper alignment, then retract and lift only a little to test retention and restore reach margin.
The holder slipped and turned sideways. Reopen and move right while leveling the wrist to improve reach and approach the holder without pushing its near face.
The holder is sideways across the jaw opening. Roll the right gripper toward a vertical pinch across its diameter, retracting slightly for clearance rather than squeezing its long ends.
Finish turning the jaws vertical and lower toward the fallen holder's diameter, keeping the right grasp open and avoiding further forward pushing.
Close the vertical pinch across the holder's body, with only a tiny forward correction, then lift and retract to check retention.
The vertical pinch passed above the holder. Reopen and lower the grasp center substantially to the visible body height, then close without pushing farther forward.
The open lower jaw contacted the table. Partially close first, then make a smaller descent while closing around the holder, followed by a short retention lift.
Use a partly open vertical pinch and small right/down corrections from the wrist view, avoiding the fully open lower jaw striking the table. Close only after this alignment.
The current pinch is constrained by the table and does not retain the holder. Lift and reposition on its right side, rotating toward an end-on recovery grasp rather than repeating the same contact.
Approach the fallen holder from its right end with a slightly downward, vertically opening grasp. Advance gradually while preserving the current elbow configuration.
Lift clear of the table and roll the right jaws toward a horizontal pinch, correcting left and back toward the holder. The vertical lower jaw was preventing a deep grasp.
Finish leveling the jaws and approach the holder's right-end body with small left/forward/down corrections, monitoring reach and table clearance.
Use the wrist view to correct toward the holder on the right side of the jaws, lower slightly at fixed orientation, and close without another large advance.
The holder is outside the right side of the grasp. Reopen and turn the fingertips toward it while retracting the wrist slightly, then lower to its side height.
Continue centering the holder in the wrist view by turning the open fingertips forward and slightly right, with a slow descent to its body height.
The holder is now centered but lies across the full horizontal opening. Shift slightly left and roll the jaws to pinch its diameter vertically, keeping clearance above the table.
The holder now overlaps the grasp depth but sits below the vertical pinch center. Reduce opening to clear the table, lower slightly, then close around its diameter.
The vertical wrist body is blocked by the table. Lift and retract it while angling the fingertips downward, so the fingers can reach below the wrist rather than forcing a lower horizontal approach.
Approach the holder's middle from above-front: shift left and forward while lowering the angled fingertips, leaving the wrist above the tabletop.
The latest approach centered the holder between the angled jaws. Close at this pose and retract with a modest lift, rather than extending farther into the reach boundary.
The head view shows the pinch still to the right of the holder. Correct substantially left across its body while reopening and descending gently; avoid repeating the same empty pinch.
The lateral alignment is improved; lower the pinch center to the holder's body height with only a very small right/forward adjustment, keeping the wrist above the table.
Reduce the opening to clear the lower jaw from the table, advance only a few millimeters into the holder's body, then close and test a short lift.
The holder remains just beyond the pinch. Make the approach shallower while moving slightly forward and toward the right-arm centerline, seeking deeper overlap without a large reach jump.
Make a final millimeter-scale advance at the current centered alignment, then close without immediately retracting so the fingers can settle around the holder's near body.
Test this deeper pinch by lifting and retracting with the right gripper closed, beginning a small uprighting rotation only as the wrist clears the table.

The lift again shows no retention. Reposition nearer the holder's center and increase the downward approach angle while retracting the wrist, so the fingertips reach the low body without the wrist hitting the table.
Advance the angled fingertips toward the holder while lowering, accounting for the short link6-to-grasp offset. Use a small right correction and stop short of any reach discontinuity.
The holder remains ahead of the fingertips. Reduce opening to clear the lower jaw and advance slowly at nearly fixed height, stopping before further extension becomes discontinuous.

With the shallower orientation providing more reach margin, advance the partly open jaws at fixed height toward the holder's near body. Check overlap before closure.
Replan from the stopped prefix: lower the grasp center with a slight wrist retraction and shallower angle, then close at the holder's near body without further extension.
The fingertips still appear above the holder's center. Use a restricted opening and lower at fixed orientation with a small right correction, then close at the lower body height.
The wrist is blocked above the table, so stop lowering against contact. Lift and retract while pitching the fingertips down, then approach the holder's near edge with the wrist safely higher.
Align the angled right fingertips farther left over the holder's near body, with a small forward/downward move. Keep the wrist orientation fixed and the jaws open for this correction.
Use the head view to bring the grasp straight forward and down toward the fallen holder's near body, keeping lateral position fixed. Close only after the short approach.
The holder is at the reach boundary. Close on its reachable near edge and retract at nearly constant low height, trying to bring it closer before attempting another lift.

Closure executed, but the first retraction was rejected. Start with submillimeter retraction increments, keeping the right gripper closed and the fingertips low to test whether the near edge can be drawn closer.
The holder did not follow the retraction. Reopen and correct the right grasp leftward toward its visible body while maintaining the recovered reach margin.

The approach reached a continuity limit. Retract slightly and ease the steep wrist angle while reducing opening, seeking a low, shallower pinch without forcing the wrist against the table.
Stop the table-constrained vertical pinch. Lift and retract while rolling to horizontal jaws, preparing to grip the holder's nearer rim/end rather than its inaccessible middle.
Finish leveling the horizontal jaws while approaching the holder's right-end rim. Lower the wrist gradually and avoid another vertical-jaw table contact.

Angle the fingertips down toward the holder while keeping the wrist higher. Advance only millimeters to stay within the current reach margin and check the diagonal pinch alignment.
Close the diagonal jaws at the current overlap and let them settle, then make a short lift and retraction to verify whether the holder follows.
